who: Marta, a freelance designer planning a long weekend in Lisbon with a friend.
goal: Wants to know what the weather will be like, see where the main sights are relative to each other, and get a few good articles to read. Needs the whole plan to still be there when she comes back later.
style: Asks follow-ups that build on earlier answers, changes her mind about dates mid-chat.
pt: Planeja uma viagem a Lisboa com clima, mapa e links, e confere depois de recarregar.

who: Daniel, a law student who got a PDF and a photo from a classmate and has to prepare for a seminar.
goal: Wants the AI to tell him what is in the PDF and the image, then compare the two in a follow-up. Wants to keep the files tied to the right chat.
style: Asks open questions, never describes the files himself, attaches the same file twice to see what happens.
pt: Estudante manda PDF e imagem e faz perguntas sobre eles em dois chats.

who: Priya, a support lead who rewrites customer emails all day and wants them consistently warm and short.
goal: Wants a reusable way to make the AI rewrite any email in her team's tone, and wants proof that it really changes the replies versus a chat without it.
style: Methodical, compares before and after, edits the instructions and tries again.
pt: Cria uma skill de revisão de e-mails e testa se ela muda de fato as respostas.

who: Tomas, a master's student keeping all research chats for his thesis on urban beekeeping in one place.
goal: Wants a home for the thesis with standing instructions the AI always follows, several chats inside it, and a clean way to tidy up when he is done.
style: Organizes obsessively, renames things, moves between projects and plain chats.
pt: Cria um projeto para a tese, com instruções, e conversa dentro dele.

who: Wei, a developer who just set up a small local tool server and wants to try it from chat.
goal: Wants to connect his local MCP server, see which tool it offers, use it from a normal conversation, and confirm the connection survives a reload and can be turned off.
style: Skeptical: checks that the tool really ran rather than trusting the reply; tries a bad URL first.
pt: Conecta o servidor MCP local e usa a ferramenta echo em conversa normal.

who: Aisha, a data analyst who suspects different models answer the same question differently.
goal: Wants to ask the same questions to each available model, switch models in the middle of a conversation without losing context, and see which one she prefers.
style: Impatient: stops replies early, regenerates, switches model while a reply is streaming.
pt: Troca de modelo no meio da conversa e compara as respostas.

who: Beatriz, a home cook in Sao Paulo who uses the app only in Brazilian Portuguese.
goal: Wants recipes in metric units, the weather for her weekend barbecue, and wants the app to remember her language and units after she closes the tab.
style: Writes in Portuguese with accents and informal slang, switches units to imperial to see the replies change.
pt: Usuária brasileira usa o app todo em português e pede receitas, tempo e medidas.

who: Kenji, a university student in Osaka who keeps notes and questions in Japanese.
goal: Wants the interface and the AI in Japanese, a few chats about his studies, and to find an old chat again by searching for a word he remembers.
style: Writes in Japanese, mixes in English words and emoji, pastes a long paragraph.
pt: Estudante japonês muda para japonês, escreve em japonês e busca no histórico.

who: Olu, a cautious user who wants a safety copy of everything before trying a new laptop.
goal: Wants to export all his data, wipe the app clean, bring everything back from the file, and be sure chats, skills and projects are all intact afterwards.
style: Careful, counts items before and after, tries importing the same file twice.
pt: Exporta os dados, apaga tudo e importa de volta, conferindo se nada se perdeu.

who: Sofia, who uses the app on her phone on the train, one-handed, in short bursts.
goal: Wants to ask quick questions, send a photo and ask about it, find her older chats from the menu, and tidy a few of them.
style: Taps fast, rotates between chats, types long messages with the on-screen keyboard.
pt: No celular, faz perguntas rápidas, anexa foto, renomeia e apaga conversas.

who: Greta, a retired teacher who likes everything set just so: dark theme, her city, her units, her name.
goal: Wants to personalize the app and see the AI actually use it, for example greeting her by name and answering weather in her units and city.
style: Changes many things quickly, reloads often, clears fields she just filled.
pt: Mexe em várias preferências ao mesmo tempo e confere se tudo persiste e se reflete no chat.

who: Hannah, a geography teacher preparing a 15-minute class activity.
goal: Wants a short quiz she can try herself, a map that shows the places from the quiz, and a summary she could hand out.
style: Answers quiz questions wrongly on purpose, asks for the same widget again with different content.
pt: Professor pede quizzes e mapas para aula e usa os widgets interativos.

who: Rafa, a power user who never touches the mouse and loves to find where software cracks.
goal: Wants to run a whole conversation, switch chats, open settings and come back using only the keyboard, while throwing odd input at it.
style: Keyboard-only, impatient, tries to break things: double sends, pasting markup, emoji, very long lines, Enter during streaming.
pt: Usuário impaciente só de teclado tenta quebrar o app com envios rápidos e textos estranhos.

who: Lena, a product manager who wants a dedicated assistant for writing release notes.
goal: Wants an assistant of her own with the right skill and model, then to use it on a real piece of text and edit it when the first result is not quite right.
style: Iterates: tweaks the setup, retries the same prompt, compares results.
pt: Cria um agente personalizado com skill e modelo próprios e conversa com ele.

who: Jonas, a consultant with a crowded week. His personal Google calendar is his main one; his employer's work calendar, jonas@northwind.test, is shared into the same Google account.
goal: Wants a free hour on Thursday for a client call that clashes with nothing in either calendar, and wants to be sure the suggestion is right before he sends the invite.
style: Plain and direct; double-checks the suggested time against both calendars; when something fails he wants to know exactly why.
facts: Connect Google as jonas@gmail.test on the fake's account chooser. All times are UTC; 'Thursday' is the next Thursday after today.

Primary calendar, Thursday: 09:00-11:00 Client workshop (Acme), 12:00-13:00 Lunch with Ana, 13:00-15:00 Proposal writing, 16:00-18:00 Quarterly planning. Free working hours there: 11:00-12:00 and 15:00-16:00. Friday is an all-day 'Conference - Lisbon'.
Work calendar jonas@northwind.test (not primary), Thursday: 15:00-16:00 Design review. So 11:00-12:00 is the only hour free in both; a suggestion of 15:00 means the work calendar was never read.

Other accounts on the chooser: no-calendar-scope@gmail.test (Calendar access not granted: Google 403 insufficientPermissions) and no-calendar-api@gmail.test (Calendar API disabled: 403 accessNotConfigured). The app should name the real cause, not a generic error.
pt: Conecta o Google e pede um horário livre na quinta que não conflite com nada na agenda pessoal nem na do trabalho.

who: Camille, a startup founder back from a week off, with her work mail in Gmail.
goal: Wants only her unread emails, ordered by how urgent they really are, then a reply draft to the most urgent one saved in Gmail so she can review and send it herself.
style: Asks for corrections to the draft, switches its tone twice, pushes back if an email she already read shows up.
facts: Connect Google as camille@gmail.test on the fake's account chooser.

8 messages from the last two days, 6 unread. Most urgent: Rita Okafor (Northstar Ventures), 'Term sheet: signature needed today by 17:00 UTC', even though Gmail does not mark it Important or starred. Next: Paul Meyer (CTO), 'Prod database at 91% disk' (marked Important), needs her OK by tomorrow; then Jana Novak asking to move Thursday's demo.
Low: Acme Tools 'ACTION REQUIRED: your 40% discount expires tonight' (marked Important and in Promotions, but marketing), a newsletter, and an HR note about next year's holiday calendar.
Already read, so never listed as unread: Paul's 'Outage last night: resolved' and Rita's 'Draft term sheet v1'.
The reply is saved as a Gmail draft (the fake stores nothing, but the tool must report it was created); it should answer Rita about the 17:00 deadline.
Other accounts on the chooser: expired@gmail.test (every call must refresh the token first) and big@gmail.test (1,200 messages).
pt: Conecta o Gmail e pede um resumo dos e-mails não lidos por urgência e um rascunho de resposta ao mais urgente.
